name: Private credit stress
value: BDC tenders above caps; ASIC stop orders
summary: Redemption limits at large private credit funds persist; Australia's ASIC issued new stop orders on 10 Nov
state: On 10 Nov Australia's regulator ASIC said complex structures, opacity and poor disclosure persist in private credit, reported six interim stop orders in total including new ones against Angas Securities, and noted redemption limits at CVS Lane (ABC News). The same report noted that US manager Blue Owl limited withdrawals in February and faced elevated redemption requests again in the June quarter. No forced asset sales or losses spreading to banks or insurers were found as of 11 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Savers in private credit funds, including through some pensions and superannuation, may face limits on how much they can withdraw each quarter. Such limits tend to persist while redemption requests stay high.
rubric_hit: Large funds limiting redemptions: Watch; no multiple simultaneous gates or bank/insurer losses for Alert

sources.title: ABC News — ASIC slams $250 billion private credit sector as risks to investors remain

why: Private credit has grown fast outside bank regulation; its losses surface late and can spill into banks, insurers and pension funds.
drivers: Defaults among leveraged mid-sized borrowers, payment-in-kind interest, fund redemption requests, bank lending to funds.

rubric.alert: Several large funds gate at once, forced asset sales, or losses spreading to banks or insurers.
rubric.watch: A large fund limits redemptions, listed BDCs trade at wide discounts to NAV, or a cluster of borrower defaults with heavy losses.
rubric.normal: No notable fund gates, defaults or markdowns beyond the routine.
